option_title: Force-field error floor for coolant MD: an enlarged C10–C50 benchmark scored against measurement
question: Does one GPU-MD force field rank C10–C50 hydrocarbons and esters in the same order as measured viscosity and thermal conductivity?
hypothesis: One TraPPE-UA Green-Kubo protocol reproduces the measured ranking of coolants because its viscosity error is a systematic bias, not a random floor.

compute_axis.quantity: benchmark molecules scored (each one independent GPU-MD run)

held_fixed: temperature 313.15 K (raised for waxy C30+ where needed)
20 ns per replicate, 5 replicates per molecule
measured values from DIPPR 801 / NIST TDE plus vendor datasheets

predictions.if_lever: The MD-vs-measurement rank correlation reaches at least 0.9 once 30+ molecules are scored, so rankings can be trusted.
predictions.if_not: The rank correlation plateaus below 0.75 even at 60 molecules, so the force-field error is a random floor.
predictions.decision_rule: Spearman rank correlation rho(MD, measured) over all scored molecules: rho >= 0.90 for viscosity and for thermal conductivity -> if_lever; rho < 0.90 -> if_not; also require rho to stop changing as the set grows 8 -> 30 -> 60.
predictions.noise_rule: Each molecule averages 5 independent seeds; a ranking change is real only if it exceeds the bootstrap 95% CI across seeds (Messerly double-exponential Green-Kubo fit).
predictions.expected_why: TraPPE-UA viscosity deviations of 20-50% can scramble close rankings, but the bias may track chain length systematically, so ranking could still hold.

compute_tested_why: Each added molecule is one independent GPU run, so more parallel GPUs/hours buy more molecules on the score axis.
scored_against: Critically evaluated measured liquid viscosity and thermal conductivity from DIPPR 801 (LVS, LTC) and NIST ThermoData Engine, plus vendor datasheets (Castrol ON DC 15, Shell MIDEL 7131) for commercial coolants.

arms.what: shear viscosity from the same Green-Kubo trajectories, compared with measured liquid viscosity
thermal conductivity from the same Green-Kubo trajectories, compared with measured liquid thermal conductivity

baseline.what: Green-Kubo MD scored against measurement exists only for a handful of molecules; Messerly et al. 2018 studied 14 normal and branched alkanes.

anchor.what: Setup reproduces published n-hexadecane Green-Kubo thermal conductivity 0.14 W/(m·K) matching its experiment, before scoring other molecules.
anchor.independent_code: GROMACS gmx energy pressure-tensor/heat-flux autocorrelation, cross-checked by a standalone Python Green-Kubo integrator

checks: Anchor: reproduce n-hexadecane thermal conductivity 0.14 W/(m·K) [s9] within ±30% before scoring any other molecule.
Per molecule: 5 independent 20-ns replicates; report bootstrap 95% CI via the double-exponential Green-Kubo fit [s1][s2].
Green-Kubo convergence: trajectory length >= ~10x the running-integral plateau time, block-averaged across seeds [s2].
Finite-size: confirm viscosity is unchanged between ~250 and ~1000 molecules before fixing the box.
Density gate: match measured liquid density within 2% at the scoring temperature before transport analysis.
Ranking: Spearman rho between MD and measured viscosity and thermal conductivity, with a bootstrap CI across seeds.
Cost guard: total GPU-hours x $1.99 <= $1,000; a timer stops the main allotment.

phases.what: Build GROMACS + TraPPE-UA setup; run 5 anchor molecules; reproduce n-hexadecane 0.14 W/(m·K); measure per-molecule throughput and error
phases.stop_rule: stop before the main spend if the anchor thermal conductivity falls below 0.10 W/(m·K)

gate.else: stop; switch force field (e.g. TAMie) and re-anchor before spending

phases.what: Run the identical protocol over the enlarged C10-C50 hydrocarbon/ester set in batches (~30, then up to 60 total), scoring each against measured values
phases.stop_rule: stop when budget_usd is exhausted or 60 molecules are scored

phases.what: Fit the error distribution, split systematic bias from random floor, compute Spearman rank correlation MD vs measured for viscosity and thermal conductivity, write report

restructuring.sequential_part: Each molecule's viscosity and thermal conductivity come from one Green-Kubo trajectory, ~50 million steps accumulated in order.
restructuring.method: None: every molecule is an independent run, so GPUs only run them side by side.

scope_gap: Cannot test whether results generalize to fluorinated or silicone coolants, other force fields, or novel-candidate discovery; only C10-C50 hydrocarbon/ester ranking.

novelty.closest_prior: Messerly 2018 scored Green-Kubo viscosity of 14 normal and branched alkanes against reference data; largest set used.
novelty.left_open: No prior work reports the force-field error distribution or rank correlation across dozens to hundreds of C10-C50 hydrocarbons and esters scored against measurement.

limits: Shows ranking reliability for one force field and one temperature; not best force field, not novel-coolant discovery, not fluorinated coolants.
test_summary: Run one GPU Green-Kubo protocol for viscosity and thermal conductivity over 60 C10-C50 hydrocarbons and esters, score against measured values, and test whether the MD ranking correlation holds as molecules are added.
